overview: Black plays 1...h6, a waiting move that gives White a free central move; the idea is to avoid Bg5 and Ng5 ideas and choose a set-up later. White usually plays 2.d4 and builds a big centre, and Black transposes to a Pirc, Modern or French-like structure. It is a throwaway first move, seldom seen above club level.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with d4 and Nc3 or Nf3.
Use the extra tempo to attack on the kingside, since h6 is a target for g4 or h4 ideas.

black_ideas.idea: Transpose to Pirc, Modern or French structures with the extra h6 move.
Challenge the centre with ...d5 or ...e5 next.

typical_structures.structure: White e4/d4 centre against a Pirc or Modern set-up with an extra ...h6.

character.notes: Slow start; the play that follows is ordinary and White just has an extra tempo.

soundness.notes: A wasted tempo, not a refutable move; Black stays playable.

structure.notes: Undecided after one move; the centre depends on which defence Black transposes into.

approach.notes: Strong players almost never play it.

level.notes: Little to memorise but no clear plan; not a first-repertoire choice.

character.reason: A quiet waiting move that leads to ordinary development.

soundness.reason: Tempo-losing but not refuted; Black can transpose into sound set-ups.

structure.reason: The centre is not decided after 1...h6.

level.reason: Little theory, but a wasted tempo is not a good first choice.

plans.reason: No defining plan; it transposes elsewhere.
